Requires division approval and licensing of food stamp vendors to the extent authorized by federal law, authorizes rulemaking and cost-linked fees, allows injunctive actions heard within twenty days of filing and service, and classifies unlicensed business as a class A misdemeanor or class E felony for a second offense within five years.

headings.title: Chapter rulemaking compliance with section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Conditions effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule promulgated under the authority of chapter 205 on promulgation pursuant to section 536.024.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.967:10887 (all five subsections, including subdivisions (1) and (2) in subsection 1) and notes (L. 1975 S.B. 255 § 1, A.L. 1981 H.B. 901; effective 6-16-81); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked section-specific definitions, stealing liability under section 570.030 covering obtaining, attempting, and aiding/abetting, 10-day reporting of new resources, prima facie evidence rule, and recovery against living recipients, estates, or dissolving corporations. Revised subsection 2 title to "Fraudulently obtaining or aiding public assistance as stealing" and expanded subsection 5 reviewNote to note corporate dissolution; retained subsections 1 and 3–5 titles.

headings.title: Definitions for public assistance fraud provisions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and notes (L. 1975 S.B. 255 § 1, A.L. 1981 H.B. 901; effective 6-16-81). Defines "public assistance benefits, programs and services" (covering chapters 198, 207, 208, 209, and 660 and department of social services programs) and "person" (individual or corporation) for this section.

headings.title: Fraudulently obtaining or aiding public assistance as stealing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Classifies obtaining, attempting to obtain, or aiding/abetting the obtaining of public assistance through willful falsehood, concealment, failure to report, impersonation, collusion, or other fraud as stealing punishable under section 570.030; revised title to capture attempts and aiding/abetting rather than only receipt.

headings.title: Reporting new income or property and benefit modification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires assistance recipients to notify their assigned case worker within ten days of receiving money, property, or income, allowing cancellation or modification after investigation if required.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence of unlawful receipt
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Makes proof of possessing disqualifying property or income prima facie evidence of unlawful receipt in recovery proceedings or criminal prosecutions.

headings.title: Recovery from estates or living ineligible recipients
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Authorizes the director of social services to recover total assistance obtained by an ineligible individual (during life or at death) or corporation (during life or at dissolution) possessing excess unreported income or property, as a seventh-class estate claim or in an action against the recipient while living.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.968:10888 (all three subsections, including subdivisions (1) and (2) and nested clauses in subsection 3) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 40 § 1 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1064); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked board powers and section 70.600 political subdivision status, subsection 2's verbatim mental-illness drafting quirk under section 630.005 ("shall not be eligible ... except that those persons may participate") without silently reconciling it, age-independent eligibility with a 16-year sheltered-workshop employment minimum, reasonable board limits, and subsection 3's verbatim "paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection" wording. Revised subsection 2 title to "Service eligibility, age rules, and board service limits" to avoid implying upper age caps; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Board creation, powers, facilities, and political subdivision status
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 40 § 1 through A.L. 2014 H.B. 1064). Requires establishing a board of directors when a section 205.971 levy is approved, empowers the board to operate section 178.900 sheltered workshops, residences, or related services, grants contracting, property, and borrowing powers (capped at published division of finance market rate), and designates the board a section 70.600 political subdivision for sections 70.600 to 70.755.

headings.title: Service eligibility, age rules, and board service limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers eligible disability categories (section 178.900, this section, developmental disability), preserves verbatim the archived source sentence stating persons with mental illness under section 630.005 "shall not be eligible... except that those persons may participate" without silently reconciling the apparent drafting discrepancy, states age-independent eligibility except a 16-year minimum for sheltered workshop employment, and allows reasonable discretionary board service limitations; revised title to avoid implying upper age limits and to distinguish board-imposed limits.

headings.title: Definitions for sections 205.968 to 205.972
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Defines "developmental disability" (including section 630.005 cross-reference; retains verbatim "paragraph (a) or (b) of this subsection" reference) and "person with a disability" for sections 205.968 to 205.972.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.969:10889 (both subsections) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 40 § 2 through A.L. 1993 S.B. 366); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked sheltered workshop and section 178.910 work/developmental program authority under DESE rules and standards in subsection 1 and residences/activity or social centers in subsection 2; retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Sheltered workshop and developmental programs under section 178.910
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 40 § 2 through A.L. 1993 S.B. 366). Permits the board to provide a sheltered workshop program and directs conducting section 178.910 work and developmental programs under department of elementary and secondary education rules and standards.

headings.title: Residences and related activity or social centers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits the board to provide residences and related activity or social centers for eligible persons.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.970:10890 (all eleven subsections, including subdivisions (1)–(3) and embedded hearing procedures in subsection 8) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 40 § 3 through A.L. 1993 S.B. 366); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked nine-member composition (noting archived "handicapped person as defined in section 205.968" phrasing), post-September 28, 1979 staggered/three-year terms, contracting/nonprofit powers, treasurer bond, section 94.645 transportation fund exception, removal grounds/hearing rules, vacancy filling, and 12-month/relative employment bars; retained all eleven drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Board appointments, qualifications, terms, and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 40 § 3 through A.L. 1993 S.B. 366). Covers appointing a nine-member board after section 205.971 voter approval (two relatives of a "handicapped person as defined in section 205.968"—noting 205.968 now uses "person with a disability"—four public members, seven residents), archived post-September 28, 1979 staggered and three-year terms, reappointment, unpaid service, and expense reimbursement.

headings.title: Facility management, personnel, quarters, and equipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Places sole administrative control and management in the board and directs employing personnel, fixing pay, and providing quarters and equipment from available funds.

headings.title: Contracting and expending funds for disability services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes contracting for related services and expending tax or other funds notwithstanding contrary law and whether or not a sheltered workshop or residence facility has been established.

headings.title: Board officers and treasurer surety bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs electing chairman, vice chairman, treasurer, and other officers, and requires a Missouri-authorized surety bond for the treasurer paid by the board before taking office.

headings.title: Admission rules and carrying out sections 205.968 to 205.972
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs the board to set facility admission rules and do all other things necessary to carry out sections 205.968 to 205.972.

headings.title: Contracts with nonprofits for common services or property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Permits contracting with not-for-profit corporations (including those implementing sections 178.900 to 178.970) for common services or common use of property.

headings.title: Gifts, property sales, and exclusive control of funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Authorizes accepting, selling, or exchanging gifts for exclusive facility benefit and grants exclusive board control over gifts, investment/sale proceeds, county tax revenues, and government grants/appropriations/loans, excepting transportation funds under section 94.645.

headings.title: Grounds and hearing procedure for removing board members
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Covers removal by majority vote of other board members after notice and hearing for five unexcused absences, prejudicial conduct, or neglect of duty, and accounts for the presiding-officer, sworn-testimony, and party-expense recording rules located inside subdivision (3).

headings.title: Reporting and filling board vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Directs the chairman to report vacancies to the mayor of a city not within a county or to the county commission/executive to be filled as original appointments, limited to the unexpired portion of an unexpired term.

headings.title: Twelve-month employment bar for former board members
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Bars individual board members from employment by the board within twelve months after ending board service.

headings.title: Employment bar for board members' relatives
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Prohibits board employment of any person related within the third degree by blood or marriage to any board member.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.972:10892 (both subsections, including the embedded official ballot table in subsection 2) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 40 § 5 through A.L. 1993 S.B. 366); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked forty-cent general levy cap versus twenty-cent cap for specified first-class charter counties and substantially required official ballot wording; retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Maximum tax rates and charter-county limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 40 § 5 through A.L. 1993 S.B. 366). Caps the tax levy at forty cents per hundred dollars assessed valuation, with a twenty-cent cap for specified first-class charter counties (containing part of a 350,000+ city or having 900,000+ population).

headings.title: Official ballot form for facility tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including the embedded ballot table and history note. Prescribes the substantially required ballot wording for establishing, improving, or maintaining sheltered workshops, residence facilities, or related services.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.979:10897 (all four subsections, including the embedded official ballot table in subsection 3), notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 5 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91), and Revisor footnote (*Words "at a" do not appear in original rolls); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked board election requests, 60-day two-newspaper notice, section 115.063 status, forty-cent cap, ballot form, and election conduct/canvassing; retained all four drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Election requests, newspaper notice, and section 115.063 status
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 5 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91), including Revisor footnote (*Words "at a" do not appear in original rolls). Covers board requests for submitting the subsection 3 proposition, 60-day legal notice in at least two newspapers, and treatment as a county or independent-city request under section 115.063.

headings.title: Maximum community mental health tax rate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Caps the community mental health tax levy at forty cents per hundred dollars assessed valuation.

headings.title: Official ballot form for community mental health tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including the embedded ballot table and notes. Sets out the substantially required official ballot form for establishing a community mental health fund and levying the tax.

headings.title: Election conduct and vote canvassing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Directs conducting the election and canvassing votes in the same manner as other county elections.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.980:10898 (all three subsections) and notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 6 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked voter-approved tax levy up to forty cents for section 205.977 purposes, Community Mental Health Fund deposit and board-approved disbursement, and continuation of an existing approved levy when a resubmitted increase/decrease fails; retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Tax levy after voter approval and rate limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 6 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91). Directs the county governing body, upon majority voter approval, to levy and collect the ballot-specified tax up to forty cents per hundred dollars assessed valuation for section 205.977 purposes.

headings.title: Tax collection and Community Mental Health Fund disbursements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Provides for collection with other county taxes, deposit into the dedicated "Community Mental Health Fund" for section 205.977 purposes only, and expenditure solely upon board of trustees approval.

headings.title: Continuation of existing levy when resubmission fails
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Keeps a previously voter-approved tax levy in effect if a resubmitted proposal to raise or lower the levy fails to receive a majority vote.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.981:10899 (all three subsections) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 7 through A.L. 1995 S.B. 454); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked board contracting with department-designated public or nonprofit providers, appropriation from community mental health or county general revenue funds capped by sections 205.977 to 205.980 tax capacity, and five-year renewable contract limits; retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Board authority to contract for mental health services
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 7 through A.L. 1995 S.B. 454). Permits the board of trustees to contract with a department-designated community mental health center, clinic, public facility, or not-for-profit corporation for mutually agreeable comprehensive mental health services for county residents.

headings.title: Funding sources and maximum contract appropriations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs appropriating contract consideration from the community mental health fund or county general revenue fund, capped at the revenue derivable from a tax levy authorized under sections 205.977 to 205.980.

headings.title: Five-year maximum contract term and renewals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Limits each service contract to a term not exceeding five years while allowing renewal from time to time.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.982:10900 (all three subsections, including subdivisions (1)–(4) in subsection 1) and notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 8 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked multicounty contractual purposes, pre-budget proportionate cost estimates (without inventing an "annual" requirement absent from the text), and withdrawal resolution/asset-debt division plan with two-year waiting period subject to funded-entity consent or unanimous participating-county vote. Revised subsection 2 to "Proportionate cost estimates for participating counties" and subsection 3 to "County withdrawal plan, consent, and two-year wait"; retained subsection 1.

headings.title: Authorized purposes of multicounty contractual agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (4) and notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 8 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91). Permits county governing bodies in a service area to contract with each other to jointly fund, supplement, purchase, or have one county operate comprehensive mental health services and facilities.

headings.title: Proportionate cost estimates for participating counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Obligates governing boards of entities receiving joint-agreement funds to submit proportionate cost estimates to each participating county prior to its budget submission date; revised title to omit "Annual" which does not appear in the statutory text.

headings.title: County withdrawal plan, consent, and two-year wait
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Covers submitting a withdrawal resolution with an equitable asset/debt adjustment plan, barring withdrawal earlier than two years without consent of funded entities unless all participating counties vote to allow earlier withdrawal; revised title to reflect the division plan and consent/unanimous-vote exceptions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.983:10901 (all three subsections) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 9, A.L. 1978 S.B. 652); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked single-county financing procedures under sections 205.977 to 205.981 for section 205.982 joint shares, joint Community Mental Health Fund deposit and board-approved disbursement, and two-surety treasurer bond filed with each participating county; retained all three drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Financing county shares of joint agreements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 9, A.L. 1978 S.B. 652). Permits any participating county to finance its share of section 205.982 joint agreements using the same single-county financing procedures under sections 205.977 to 205.981.

headings.title: Joint Community Mental Health Fund deposit and disbursement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs depositing moneys received from participating counties into a special "Community Mental Health Fund" and disbursing them with board approval under the joint agreements.

headings.title: Treasurer bond requirements for participating counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the board treasurer, before receiving county funds, to execute a board-approved bond with two or more sureties to each participating county and file it with each county.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.984:10902 (all four subsections, including subdivisions (1) and (2) in subsection 4) and notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 10 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked nine-member minimum, section 632.040 nominations, archived one-year post-January 1, 1991 appointment timeline, one-third provider/consumer ratios, funded-entity employee bar, demographic representation, licensed physician and at-least-one-half nonprovider requirement, multicounty apportionment, and staggered three-year terms. Revised subsection 2 title to "Demographic representation, physician, and nonprovider minimum" because at least one-half is not a majority on even-numbered boards; retained subsections 1, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Board size, nominations, composition limits, and employee bar
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 10 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91). Covers minimum nine-member board, nominations by the section 632.040 regional advisory council or interested parties, archived appointment deadline within one year of January 1, 1991, one-third provider cap, one-third consumer/family minimum, and prohibition on employees of entities funded under sections 205.975 to 205.990.

headings.title: Demographic representation, physician, and nonprovider minimum
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires board composition to reflect service-area resident demographics, include at least one licensed physician, and have at least one-half non-health-care providers; revised title to replace "majority" with "minimum" because one-half is not a majority on even-numbered boards.

headings.title: County representation in multicounty service areas
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Guarantees at least one board representative for each participating county in a multicounty service area, with remaining members apportioned by county population.

headings.title: Three-year terms and initial staggered terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and notes. Establishes three-year terms and sets staggered one-, two-, and three-year initial appointment schedules for multicounty and single-county service areas.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.985:10903 (both subsections) and notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 11 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked preserved validity and optional reconstitution of pre-existing designated providers/governing boards and permitted board contracting with existing public or nonprofit providers under sections 205.975 to 205.990; retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Validity and possible reconstitution of existing providers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 11 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91). Preserves the validity of pre-existing department-designated community mental health centers, providers, and their governing boards without precluding reconstitution to include all or part of the board of trustees.

headings.title: Permitted contracts with existing public or nonprofit providers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Clarifies that nothing in sections 205.975 to 205.990 precludes a county or multicounty service-area board from contracting with an existing public facility or not-for-profit organization for comprehensive mental health services.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.987:10905 (both subsections) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 13, A.L. 1978 S.B. 652); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked distinct applicability of department-promulgated construction/staffing/operation/service standards and annual review/inspection for local sections 205.975 to 205.990 fund disbursement (subsection 1) versus federal community mental health grant applicants (subsection 2); retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Department standards and annual review for local-funded entities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 168 § 13, A.L. 1978 S.B. 652). Distinguished from subsection 2 by directing the department (in consultation with the state advisory council and existing providers) to set construction, staffing, operation, and service standards required before disbursing sections 205.975 to 205.990 funds, with annual department review or inspection.

headings.title: Department standards and annual review for federal-grant applicants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 1 by requiring entities applying for federal community mental health grants to meet department-promulgated construction, staffing, operation, and maintenance standards and undergo annual department review and inspection.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.989:10907 (both subsections) and history note (L. 1978 S.B. 652); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked prohibition on denying county-established or county-funded sections 205.975 to 205.990 mental health services for inability to pay in subsection 1 and ability-to-pay charges tied to actual inpatient/outpatient/examination/other service costs in subsection 2; retained both drafted titles as accurate.

headings.title: Prohibition on denying services for inability to pay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1978 S.B. 652). Prohibits denying services due to inability to pay at any center, clinic, public facility, or nonprofit where counties have established services or provided funds under sections 205.975 to 205.990.

headings.title: Ability-to-pay charges tied to actual service costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs charging recipients of comprehensive mental health services funded in whole or part under sections 205.975 to 205.990 based on ability to pay and related to actual inpatient, outpatient, examination, or other service costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read complete archived version 205.990:10908 (all three subsections, including subdivisions (1) and (2) in subsection 3) and notes (L. 1978 S.B. 652, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked charging nonparticipating service-area counties for residents unable to pay, proportionate actual-cost calculation matching participating counties' expense share, and primary-residence rules for services with versus without nighttime sleeping accommodations. Revised subsection 1 title to "Charging nonparticipating counties for residents unable to pay" to follow the statute's own phrasing; retained subsections 2 and 3.

headings.title: Charging nonparticipating counties for residents unable to pay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1978 S.B. 652, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1383; effective 1-1-91). Requires a center or clinic supported by some but not all counties in a service area to charge nonparticipating counties for services rendered to their residents not able to pay; revised title to follow the statutory "unable to pay" phrasing rather than introducing "indigent".

headings.title: Proportionate cost calculation for nonparticipating counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Ties nonparticipating-county charges to the same proportion of actual inpatient, outpatient, examination, or other service costs as the proportion of actual service expenses borne by participating counties.

headings.title: Determining county of residence for service recipients
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and notes. Defines county of residence for this section as primary residence at entry for services with nighttime sleeping accommodations, and primary residence for services without nighttime sleeping accommodations.
